name: IARU Region 2 (the Americas)
source: IARU Region 2 Band Plan, September 2020. iaru-r2.org. 2 m, 70 cm and 23 cm: IARU Region 2 Band Plan, September 2020 edition (the current PDF on the site, file dated 18 October 2022, title page unchanged); iaru-r2.org. Receiver bands (not amateur): summarised from the ITU Radio Regulations Article 5 table of allocations and general knowledge of national use. Broad, and not specific to a licence.
note: A regional plan for any country in Region 2 without its own file here. Many countries don't allow all of 80 m, 40 m or 60 m: copy this file and edit it for your country. On VHF and UHF: A voluntary regional guide: national and local plans may differ, so check them before transmitting. 2 m is primary exclusive in Region 2. 70 cm is secondary (fixed, mobile and radiolocation among the primary users) and so is 23 cm (radiolocation primary, plus radionavigation satellite on 1240-1260 MHz). Some countries lack the full 430-450 MHz, and the IC-9700 tunes 430-450 only. The plan allows DV in its FM, DV segments and names no digital-voice calling frequency on these bands, and gives no FM calling frequency on 70 cm. FT8, FT4, MSK144, Q65 and WSPR markers are WSJT-X defaults, not plan frequencies. The non-amateur bands are only offered on a receiver, and a guide to what's where, not a statement of who may use it.
